Mali report 2: Mali: more than 2,400 schools remain closed as insecurity disrupts new school year. Summary: Mali's new school year began Thursday with more than 2,400 schools unable to reopen, as worsening insecurity and the growing presence of jihadist groups continue to disrupt education. The 2026-2027 academic year has been declared the “Year of Education and Culture” by President Assimi Goïta, but thousands of children are starting the year without access to their classrooms.

Burkina Faso report 2: Fight against fraud and clandestine gold mining: Condor Authority and its men strike hard. Summary: The Water and Forestry Combatant Unit based in Djikologo (Djôrô, former south-west of Burkina Faso) conducted, from 26 to 27 September 2026, a series of operations against illicit trafficking, fraud and clandestine gold mining. These operations have achieved significant results, illustrating the determination of agents to protect natural resources, preserve the environment and enforce the law .
Burkina Faso report 3: Burkina Faso's military leaders mark four years in power. Summary: People gathered in Ougadougou’s Place de la Révolution on Wednesday night to mark four years since Captain Ibrahim Traoré came to power in a coup. The culmination of anniversary celebrations, they paid tribute to the armed forces and the military government’s achievements in Burkina Faso. One resident, Abdoul Rasmané Sawadogo, said military leaders have created an “ultra-modern army that meets expectations”.

articles.title: Defence in Burkina Faso: 250 billion FCFA collected in nine months by the Patriotic Support Fund
articles.summary: The Patriotic Support Fund (FSP) mobilized 250,158,437,479 FCFA as of September 29, 2026, or 125.08% achievement rate for an annual target of 200 billion FCFA. These figures were presented on 30 September in Ouagadougou by Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo at the third ordinary session 2026 of the Fund's Policy Board . The Burkinabe government has made strengthening its defence capabilities a priority in recent years.

articles.title: Pix of the Day, 30 September, 2026 - Across the world
articles.summary: Burkina Faso has inaugurated its first gold refinery as its military-led government seeks to strengthen economic sovereignty after breaking ties with its traditional Western partners. “From now on, Burkina Faso’s gold must not only be mined in Burkina Faso; it must also be processed, controlled, valued and certified there,” President Ibrahim Traoré said on Monday at the inauguration of the refinery, named Raffinor-BF.

articles.title: Crash of the Ouagadougou-Alger flight: Swiftair condemned
articles.summary: The families of the victims had to wait twelve years. Gathered within the association "AH-5017 Ensemble", they led a "relentless fight for truth and justice" which is now experiencing its judicial outcome. The Spanish company Swiftair is found guilty of manslaughter this Monday morning by the Paris Criminal Court .

articles.title: Niger: Islamic State claims responsibility for attack on Niamey airport
articles.summary: Published on Friday, January 30, 2026 | AFP The Islamic State claimed responsibility on Friday for the attack on Niamey airport in Niger, said the Site group, which specializes in counter-terrorism research . On the night of Wednesday to Thursday, Niamey airport, which is home to military sites and is about ten kilometers from the presidency, was the target of an attack leaving 20 dead on the attacking side, according to the Nigerien military junta .
